olivia (sec-eng): Heads up — since this morning we're seeing intermittent SAML assertion decrypt failures for a handful of customers in EU. Customer report: login 500 -> 'decrypt failed'.

sam (infra-kms): Noted. Any correlation with the KMS key rotation earlier? I ran a quick check and the rotation completed at 05:12 UTC.

olivia (sec-eng): Possibly. Logs show the Assertion encrypted element fails with 'invalid JWE header' for some assertions but others succeed. Strange part: KMS audit shows successful decrypts around the same times.

anita (identity): Can you paste the raw log snippet? Also did anything change in the SAML attribute encryption config or the SP metadata?

olivia (sec-eng): Paste below — obfuscated tenant ids:

```
time=2026-02-10T05:33:21Z level=error svc=sp-decrypt tenant=tenant-az1 err="jwe: unsupported header alg 'A256GCM'" request_id=abc123
time=2026-02-10T05:33:21Z level=info svc=kms tenant=tenant-az1 action=Decrypt key=projects/redwood/keys/idp-wrap key_version=7 status=ok req=abc123
```

olivia (sec-eng): So SP saw unsupported header alg but KMS says decrypt OK for the same request id. That suggests our JWE parsing layer rejected the assertion before KMS gets engaged for some code path.

sam (infra-kms): That aligns with a library bump we did in sp-decrypt last week (bumped jose lib). It added stricter header validation and dropped fallback for A256GCM -> A256GCMKW mismatch. I flagged it in the changelog but didn't expect prod impact.

ryan (sre): We also rolled an RBAC change yesterday: new minimal-role for service accounts. Could that affect the SP pod's ability to call the KMS key version? KMS logs look fine but maybe we hit a permission check in our middleware.

anita (identity): I doubt RBAC on the SP pod would cause a header parse error. More likely the assertion encryption algorithm coming from certain IdPs changed to a variant our parser no longer accepts. Did we see changes on the IdP side or a federated partner update?

olivia (sec-eng): Customer says their IdP didn't change. However, a couple tenants on older ES-2 connectors started failing while newer ones OK. Could be connector translation.

sam (infra-kms): Actionable plan: 1) roll back the jose lib bump in staging and run repro. 2) add additional debug logging in sp-decrypt to dump JWE headers (safe-mask keys). 3) sanity-check RBAC: confirm the SP service account still has kms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt for key version=7.

ryan (sre): I'll verify RBAC in parallel. If permissions are fine, we can test local repro with their assertion.

anita (identity): I'll ask the customer for a sample (redacted) assertion and their connector version. Also checking our SCIM provisioning logs — unrelated but FYI we had a burst of 403s earlier, might be linked to a misrouted token.

olivia (sec-eng): Quick mitigation: temporarily enable a permissive header fallback in sp-decrypt to accept the A256GCM header until we patch the parser. We should gate by tenant so only affected customers see it. Thoughts?

sam (infra-kms): That seems reasonable as a canary. Minimal change: if header.alg=="A256GCM" and key wrap present, accept. I'll author a tiny patch.

ryan (sre): If we do that, let's deploy to a small subset of EU nodes and monitor KMS errors, latency, and audit logs. Deploy-bot — can you spin a canary group for sp-decrypt EU1 with tag canary/kms-header-fallback?

deploy-bot: CI passed. Deploy queued for canary/kms-header-fallback -> targeting 3 pods in eu-west-1. Will report health checks at +5m and +15m. :rocket:

olivia (sec-eng): Thanks. Also logging item: our audit pipeline doesn't currently surface JWE parse rejects as an SSO+audit event. Can we add a metric/alert for parse failures so we detect this class faster?

anita (identity): Agreed — that would help. I'll open an eval ticket to add parse_failure counter + alert if >10/min per region.

sam (infra-kms): Patch PR: https://git.internal/redwood/sp-decrypt/pull/824 (adds header fallback + debug logging). Repro steps in PR description.

ryan (sre): RBAC check done — SP service account still has required KMS perms. No recent role changes affecting it.

olivia (sec-eng): Outcome: canary shows errors drop for tenant-az1 after canary applied. We should schedule a proper library fix (strip unsupported header variants, canonicalize alg names) and follow-up: 1) harden parsing, 2) add audit metric, 3) postmortem with IDP connector owners.

anita (identity): Filing postmortem and notifying affected customers.

olivia (sec-eng): Assigning owners: sam -> patch & release; anita -> customer comms + postmortem; ryan -> monitoring + RBAC verification; olivia -> incident writeup. I'll update once postmortem draft is up. :white_check_mark:
